title: Rivers and Mountains
intro: A wander across the map, following rivers and climbing peaks. Take your time.

questions.prompt: Which mountain has the highest peak above sea level?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest, on the border of Nepal and China, rises about 8,849 metres above sea level.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range is often used as part of the boundary between Europe and Asia?
questions.explanation: The Ural Mountains run north to south through Russia and are traditionally treated as part of the divide between the two continents.

questions.prompt: Which is the longest mountain range on land?
questions.explanation: The Andes stretch about 7,000 kilometres along the west side of South America.

questions.prompt: Into which sea does the Nile flow at its end?
questions.explanation: The Nile flows north through Egypt and ends in a wide delta where it meets the Mediterranean Sea.

questions.prompt: Most of the Amazon River flows through which country?
questions.explanation: The Amazon carries more water than any other river, and the largest part of its basin and its course lies in Brazil.
The Seine winds through the middle of Paris on its way to the English Channel.

questions.prompt: Which river flows from the Alps to the North Sea?
questions.explanation: The Rhine begins in the Swiss Alps and runs through or beside several countries before reaching the North Sea in the Netherlands.

questions.prompt: The Mississippi River ends in a wide delta in which US state?
questions.explanation: The Mississippi flows south through the middle of the United States and reaches the sea in southern Louisiana.

questions.prompt: Which is the highest mountain in Africa?
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro in Tanzania rises about 5,895 metres. It stands alone rather than in a range.

questions.prompt: Where is the mouth of a river?
choices: Where it meets a sea, lake or larger river
questions.explanation: The source is where a river starts and the mouth is where it ends, flowing into a sea, a lake or another river.

questions.prompt: In which country is Mount Fuji?
questions.explanation: Mount Fuji, a snow-capped volcano, is the highest mountain in Japan at about 3,776 metres.
